sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian verbs change according to the subject. Common first-person forms end in -ok/-ek/-ök, chosen the same way a plural or any other suffix is — by vowel harmony.

-ok, -ek, -ök are yet another vowel-harmony family, just like the -ban/-ben suffix you’ve already met — back-vowel verbs take -ok, front-vowel verbs split between -ek and -ök. Tanulok fits this cleanly: back-vowel tanul, so -ok. The pattern you’re building for nouns applies to verbs too.
